away.name: Stuart Skinner
away.news: Impressive early-season performances from Stuart Skinner and Clay Stevenson made Connor Hellebuyck's (suspension) absence an afterthought, but recent struggles are keeping Winnipeg's crease uncertain. That said, even in a 2-1 loss to the St. Louis Blues in his previous game, Skinner played well, stopping 26 of 28 shots (.929 SV%). The 27-year-old Canadian goalie has a 2.65 GAA and .910 SV% in six games (3-1-2). The Jets enter Thursday's game as +174 road underdogs against a Dallas Stars team with points in six of its last seven games (5-1-1).

home.name: Jake Oettinger
home.news: The Stars have struggled offensively at times to start the season, but they can point to Jake Oettinger's outstanding play as the reason for their 5-3-1 record. In seven games this season (4-2-1), the 27-year-old Oettinger has already posted three shutouts, with an outstanding 1.13 GAA and .945 SV%. He saved 18 of 20 shots (.900 SV%) in his previous game, a 3-2 overtime win over the Boston Bruins. The Stars enter Thursday's divisional clash as sizeable -196 home favourites against a Winnipeg Jets team that has scored two or fewer goals in three of their last five games (1-3-1).

away.name: Jesper Wallstedt
away.news: Wallstedt has been busy with Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined and will return to the crease for the 10th time in Minnesota's first 11 games. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie has given Head Coach John Hynes no reason to deviate, posting a solid 2.20 GAA and .915 SV% in nine games (6-1-2). That said, he is coming off his weakest performance of the season, allowing four goals on 32 shots (.875 SV%) in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Edmonton Oilers. Minnesota enters Thursday's contest as significant -202 road favourites against a Calgary Flames team coming off an impressive 3-2 win over the Carolina Hurricanes.

home.name: Devin Cooley
home.news: Cooley had a terrific first season as a full-time NHLer, serving primarily as Dustin Wolf's backup, posting a solid 2.69 GAA and .909 SV% in 31 appearances (10-10-6) for a poor Calgary Flames team. The 29-year-old Cooley struggled in his first two 2026-27 outings, but was excellent in his most recent game, saving 34 of 36 shots (.944 SV%) in a 3-2 win over the Carolina Hurricanes. He has a 4.01 GAA and .868 SV% in three games (1-2-0). The Flames enter Thursday's action as +180 home underdogs against a Minnesota Wild team on a three-game winning streak.

away.name: Brandon Bussi
away.news: The Hurricanes have leaned on Kochetkov for four of their last five games, but they will turn to Bussi on Thursday against the Edmonton Oilers. Bussi emerged from nowhere as a 27-year-old rookie in the 2025-26 season, leading the Hurricanes to a Stanley Cup, but he hasn't recaptured that brilliance in 2026-27. He has a 2.98 GAA and .882 SV in five games (2-2-1). The Hurricanes enter Thursday's contest as -117 road favourites against a 7-1-1 Oilers team.

home.name: Devon Levi
home.news: Heading into the 2026-27 season, the Oilers were turning to a goaltending tandem of Frederik Andersen and Tristan Jarry, but an injury to Andersen created an opening for Levi, who is making the most of his opportunity. Levi is coming off a strong performance, saving 37 of 30 shots (.900 SV%) in a 4-3 win over the Minnesota Wild. The 24-year-old goalie has a 2.00 GAA and .931 SV% in his last five games (4-1-0). The Oilers enter Thursday's contest as slight +106 home underdogs against a Carolina Hurricanes team that is 8-1-0 in their last nine games.
